accepted.passageWithMarkers: Scientists have no special purchase on moral or ethical decisions; a climate scientist is no more qualified __(A) to comment__ on health care reform than a physicist is to judge the causes of bee colony collapse. The very features that create expertise in a specialized domain __(B) leading__ to ignorance in many others. In some cases lay people ― farmers, fishermen, patients, native peoples ― may have relevant experiences __(C) that__ scientists can learn from. Indeed, in recent years, scientists have begun to recognize this: the Arctic Climate Impact Assessment includes observations __(D) gathered__ from local native groups. So our trust needs to be limited, and focused. It needs to be very particular. Blind trust will get us into at least __(E) as much trouble as__ no trust at all. But without some degree of trust in our designated experts ― the men and women who have devoted their lives to sorting out tough questions about the natural world we live in ― we are paralyzed, in effect not knowing whether to make ready for the morning commute or not.

accepted.passageWithMarkers: Gaining an audience for your writing involves not just finding a voice but ensuring that voice __(A) resonating__ with your intended readers. Entrepreneurs understand the importance of building a brand __(B) that__ makes them memorable and distinct from their competitors, __(C) drawing__ customers to their products or services. They achieve this by pinpointing their target audience, crafting a unique value proposition, and shaping a recognizable identity. While scholars might initially find these entrepreneurial concepts __(D) alien__, they actually engage in similar practices when they set themselves apart in their academic writing. Consider the typical literature review and motivation section of a scholarly article ― the aim is to highlight gaps in existing research and position oneself as the one __(E) who__ will address these overlooked areas. The challenge, as Labaree suggests, is not just in developing innovative ideas but in cultivating a distinctive voice that makes readers think, "Ah, this sounds like [the author]." It's about balancing the expression of your ideas with the development of a unique voice that leaves a temporary impression on your audience.

accepted.passageWithMarkers: Learning a second language is easiest during early childhood. When children are __(A) exposed__ to two different languages from birth, they generally become native speakers of both. Adults, on the other hand, rarely attain the fluency of a native speaker in a second language. There is, however, some concern that bilingualism can cause problems for children. This is partly due to something __(B) called__ “code-switching,” which occurs when bilingual people mix two languages together. But code-switching can also be viewed as an extra ability that gives bilingual children cognitive advantages over their peers. Unlike other children, bilingual kids have another language __(C) from that__ they can retrieve a word if they can’t remember it in the first. Furthermore, shifting back and forth between languages can make it easier for them __(D) to switch__ between tasks, __(E) leading__ to superior problem-solving skills. So, although it may lead to moments of confusion, bilingualism could ultimately give children an advantage in terms of overall cognitive abilities.

carry American structural methods back into surviving Formalist circles in Europe
adapt Czech pedagogical models for use in Harvard and MIT classrooms
merge European and American schools into one continuous linguistic tradition
extend structural linguistics into anthropology, art criticism, and brain research

wrongOptionExplanations.4: 양 대륙 경험으로 '통합'을 떠올리기 쉽지만, 지문은 간극을 이은 가교 역할이지 두 학파를 하나의 연속 전통으로 합쳤다고 말하지 않는다.
wrongOptionExplanations.5: 말미의 인류학·예술비평·뇌 연구 영향이 그대로 보이지만, 그것은 이론 파급의 귀결이며 빈칸의 유럽–미국 언어학 간 연결 명제와 층위가 다르다.

accepted.explanation: 빈칸 문장은 야콥슨이 미국에서 가르친 결과가 글 전체 경력을 어떻게 의미화하는지를 보여주는 인과 귀결부다. 앞부분은 그가 러시아 형식주의와 프라하 언어학 서클의 유럽 전통을 지닌 채, 나치 침공 뒤 미국으로 건너와 뉴욕 언어학 서클과 하버드·MIT에서 가르친 과정을 제시한다. 이 두 근거를 이으면 가르침으로 이룬 바는 유럽 언어학 전통을 미국 학계에 옮겨 양쪽을 이은 역할로 재진술된다. ①이 그 종합이다. ②는 유럽→미국 방향의 전도, ③은 교수법으로의 과협소, ④는 가교를 완전 통합으로 과장한 범위 비틀기, ⑤는 말미 타 학문 파급을 빈칸 명제에 대입한 절반-진실이다.

options.text: hinges more on guiding the child's emotions into calm than on mastering our own responses
consists less in correcting the child's conduct than in regulating the self
is less about constructive replies under pressure than about shielding kids from hard obstacles
unfolds within the parent chiefly once childish storms have already passed
matters mainly as parents model peace while the growth remains the child's task

wrongOptionExplanations.1: calm·emotions·responses 개념을 빌려 매력적이나, 자녀 정서를 이끄는 쪽이 더 본질이라 하여 자기 응답 통제가 핵심인 논지를 주체 전도로 뒤집는다.
wrongOptionExplanations.3: constructive reply·obstacles를 본문에서 가져왔지만, 통제 불가능한 장애물 차단을 응답보다 우선하여 글이 부정한 통제 환상을 복원한다.
wrongOptionExplanations.4: within the parent와 storms를 엮어 절반만 맞지만, 폭풍이 지나간 뒤에야 성립한다고 하여 폭풍 속에서 성찰·응답하는 성장 논지를 시점상 어긋나게 한다.

accepted.explanation: 빈칸 문장은 양육의 본령이 어디에 있는지를 규정하는 핵심 논지 진술이다. 앞부분에서 부모는 자녀나 장애물을 통제할 수 없고 자신의 행동만 통제할 수 있으며, 양육은 자녀가 무엇을 하느냐가 아니라 부모가 어떻게 응답하느냐에 달렸다고 했다. 이어 버튼이 눌릴 때 반사적으로만 반응하지 말고 성찰하여 평형을 되찾는 내적 성장이 더 평화로운 부모가 되게 한다고 수렴한다. 따라서 빈칸은 양육이 자녀 교정보다 자기 조율에 있다는 뜻으로 재구성되어 ②가 된다. ①은 자녀 정서 유도에 무게를 두는 주체 전도, ③은 장애물 차단을 우선하는 범위 비틀기, ④는 폭풍 이후만 부모 내부라는 시점 오류, ⑤는 성장 과업을 자녀에게 돌리는 오귀속이다.
keyPoints: 양육의 핵심은 자녀 통제가 아니라 부모 자신의 정서·행동 관리
버튼이 눌릴 때의 성찰이 내적 성장을 가능하게 한다
자녀 행동·장애물 제거를 전제로 한 선지는 핵심 논지와 어긋난다
accepted.passageWithBlank: Most parents think that if our child would just "behave," we could stay calm as parents. The truth is that managing our own emotions and actions is what allows us to feel peaceful as parents. Ultimately we can't control our children or the obstacles they will face - but we can always control our own actions. Parenting isn't about what our child does, but about how we respond. In fact, most of what we call parenting _____. When a storm brews, a parent's response will either calm it or trigger a full-scale tsunami. Staying calm enough to respond constructively to all that childish behavior - and the stormy emotions behind it - requires that we grow, too. If we can use those times when our buttons get pushed to reflect, not just react, we can notice when we lose equilibrium and steer ourselves back on track. This inner growth is the hardest work there is, but it's what enables you to become a more peaceful parent, one day at a time.

accepted.explanation: 빈칸 문장은 개인성 강조가 문제라는 필자 결론의 핵심 귀결을 담당한다. 앞에서 대규모 작업에서는 상당수 디자이너가 개념 구현에 고용되어 개인 기여가 쉽게 간과된다고 했고, 그룹으로 일할 때 관리 조직과 과정이 창의성 못지않게 중요할 수 있다고 했다. 이 두 근거를 잇면 성공한 디자이너 ‘개인성’들은 실제 단독 디자인보다 팀의 개념 구현을 조율하는 리더로 주로 기능한다는 뜻이므로 ②가 정답이다. ①은 손작업 철수로 과장했고, ③은 기술 복잡도라는 지엽 조건으로 축소했으며, ④·⑤는 개인 감각을 관리보다 앞세우는 극성 반전이다.

accepted.passageWithBlank: A striving to demonstrate individual personality through designs should not be surprising. Most designers are educated to work as individuals, and design literature contains countless references to 'the designer'. Personal flair is without doubt an absolute necessity in some product categories, particularly relatively small objects, with a low degree of technological complexity, such as furniture, lighting, small appliances, and housewares. In larger-scale projects, however, even where a strong personality exercises powerful influence, the fact that substantial numbers of designers are employed in implementing a concept can easily be overlooked. The emphasis on individuality is therefore problematic ― rather than actually designing, many successful designer 'personalities' _____. A distinction needs to be made between designers working truly alone and those working in a group. In the latter case, management organization and processes can be equally as relevant as designers' creativity.
